title: Early internal response predicts later hair-output trajectory
question: Does an early intervention-linked internal-state response improve prediction of later hair output beyond baseline visible output?

variables.delta_z_early: early change in candidate internal-state probe
variables.delta_H_late: later change in visible hair output

models.M1: delta_H_late ~ H0 + declared baseline covariates + delta_z_early

acceptance: M1 improves held-out predictive performance relative to M0
predictive direction replicates in at least one independent intervention-linked dataset
analysis preserves subject-level grouping and prevents leakage
uncertainty and sensitivity analysis are reported
non_acceptance: post-hoc biomarker selection after outcome inspection
in-sample fit improvement without held-out validation
single uncontrolled small cohort as sole evidence

seed_evidence.citation: Tang et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2003
seed_evidence.candidate_probe: dermal-papilla IGF-1 mRNA change at 4 months

seed_evidence.citation: Mirmirani et al., Br J Dermatol 2015
seed_evidence.role: controlled feasibility of intervention-linked transcriptome and hair-output observation

claim_boundary: Passing HF-VAL-002 would validate predictive value of a declared early-response probe in declared datasets; it would not establish treatment efficacy, consciousness-driven recovery, or a universal biological recoverability variable.
